label: Early original-phase positions (t=1-4), keyed by token identity (after h/u/v/i/x/n, or on n/f/s)
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, at early positions t=1..5 (t=2 peaks, 46% of mass; t=1-3 hold 94% of mass, t=1-4 hold 99.5%). Never at t=0, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (8 of 546k copy steps). Inside that window, whether it fires and how strongly depends on token identity: it is much more likely after h, u, v, i, x, n (prev_tok lift about 3x) and on input n, f, s (in_tok lift 2.2-3.3x). The strongest activations are on n right after h/u, e.g. v h u [n] and h h [n]. Mostly on the first occurrence of a token (89% of mass). The position window alone gets recall 0.91 but precision 0.20; adding the token sets raises dev F1 to 0.54 (P 0.48, R 0.63, mass recall 0.74). The rest of the token dependence looks like a graded mix of the current and earlier tokens (first_tok also matters) that no simple set captures.
